summary: @hubsync/web-sdk-react preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package declares itself as 'Verdocs Web SDK for React' under an unrelated @hubsync scope while the bundled dist references verdocs.com endpoints, matching an impersonation shape. On `npm install`, the declared `preinstall` script `node setup.mjs` downloads the Bun standalone runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, marks it executable, then invokes it via `execFileSync` to run the sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727 KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` blob with a rotated string-array / index-lookup dispatcher (`WV8StW`, `n7gIxM`, `hc1jfK9`) and no readable API surface, unrelated to any advertised React SDK functionality. The payload is not Node-resolvable and is only executed through the freshly-downloaded alien runtime, which conceals its behavior from Node-based inspection while still running with full user privilege at install time. This matches the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: Bun itself is legitimate, but its role here is to execute an obfuscated, unrelated-to-purpose payload rather than the package's own shipped code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
